sections.content: When most investors think about hot real estate markets, they picture Phoenix, Atlanta, or Tampa. Bismarck, North Dakota rarely makes that list. But that's exactly why savvy investors are paying attention. Real estate deals in Bismarck ND offer something increasingly rare in today's market: affordability, stable demand, and low competition from other investors. Whether you're a first-time investor or an experienced wholesaler looking to diversify, Bismarck deserves a serious look. If you're just getting started, check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in.
Bismarck ND Real Estate Market Overview

Bismarck is the state capital of North Dakota and home to roughly 75,000 residents. It sits along the Missouri River and serves as the economic and government hub for the western half of the state. The local economy is driven by state government jobs, healthcare, energy, and agriculture — all sectors that tend to be recession-resistant. That economic stability translates directly into a housing market that doesn't see the wild swings you get in speculative Sun Belt markets. Median home prices in Bismarck currently sit around $285,000 to $310,000, which is significantly below the national median. Days on market typically run 30 to 50 days, giving investors time to do proper due diligence without feeling rushed.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Bismarck
Not all zip codes in Bismarck are created equal for investors. The city has a mix of older established neighborhoods and newer suburban growth corridors, each offering different opportunity types.
North Bismarck and the Airport District

North Bismarck is one of the most active areas for fix-and-flip investors. Homes here were largely built between the 1950s and 1980s, meaning there's a consistent supply of properties that need cosmetic updates. Purchase prices in this corridor often range from $160,000 to $220,000 for distressed properties, with after-repair values (ARVs) landing between $250,000 and $290,000. That spread creates workable margins for flippers who keep rehab budgets tight. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to quickly estimate your upside on any North Bismarck deal before making an offer.
South Bismarck and the Highway 83 Corridor

South Bismarck is where the city's growth is happening. New construction is active, but so is demand for existing rentals near major employers like Sanford Health and the state capitol complex. Single-family rentals in this area typically rent for $1,200 to $1,600 per month, and well-priced buy-and-hold properties can generate gross rent multipliers in the 12 to 15 range — solid numbers for a mid-sized Midwest market.
The Older Downtown-Adjacent Neighborhoods

Streets within a mile or two of downtown Bismarck offer interesting wholesale opportunities. Many homes were built before 1960 and are owned by long-term residents or inherited by heirs who may have little interest in managing or maintaining them. These are classic motivated seller situations that wholesalers and direct mail investors look for.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Bismarck ND
Wholesaling

Wholesaling is a viable strategy in Bismarck, though the market is smaller than a major metro. The key is finding motivated sellers before other investors do. Probate properties, pre-foreclosures, and absentee-owner homes in aging neighborhoods are your best sources. Assignment fees in Bismarck typically run between $8,000 and $20,000 depending on the deal. Because the investor pool here is smaller, competition for deals is lower than in a market like Minneapolis or Denver. Learn how to source these opportunities in our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals).
Fix and Flip

Bismarck's fix-and-flip market is steady rather than explosive. Flippers who do well here focus on light-to-medium rehabs in the $20,000 to $50,000 range and target the $250,000 to $325,000 price point where buyer demand is strongest. Avoid over-improving properties — Bismarck buyers are practical and won't pay a premium for luxury finishes in a working-class neighborhood. Labor and material costs are moderate compared to coastal markets, which helps protect margins. A realistic net profit on a well-executed Bismarck flip ranges from $25,000 to $55,000.
Buy-and-Hold Rentals

This is arguably the strongest long-term play in Bismarck. The city has a healthy renter population — roughly 35% of households rent — fueled by college students, young professionals, and energy sector workers who rotate in and out of the region. Vacancy rates have held below 5% for most of the past five years. A three-bedroom single-family home purchased for $220,000 can rent for $1,300 to $1,500 per month, producing a cap rate in the 5% to 7% range depending on your financing. That's not a home run, but it's consistent cash flow with appreciation potential.

Bismarck Real Estate Market Trends to Watch in 2024

items: Inventory remains tight: Active listings in Bismarck have been running 20% to 30% below historical averages, which supports home values even as interest rates stay elevated.
New construction is active but focused on the $350,000+ range, leaving a gap in affordable starter homes that investors can fill.
Population growth is modest but consistent, averaging around 1% per year, driven by in-migration from rural North Dakota counties.
The energy sector — particularly oil and natural gas activity in western ND — continues to send temporary workers to Bismarck, supporting short-term rental demand.
Interest rate sensitivity is real: higher rates have cooled buyer demand at the margins, creating more negotiating room for cash investors.
Rental rates have increased roughly 6% to 8% over the past 18 months, improving cash-on-cash returns for landlords who purchased 2 to 3 years ago.

sections.content: How to Analyze Deals in Bismarck Like a Pro

Deal analysis in a smaller market like Bismarck requires a slightly different lens than you'd use in a major metro. Comparable sales can be thin, neighborhoods shift quickly over just a few blocks, and you'll want to account for North Dakota's harsh winters in your rehab budget (roof, HVAC, insulation, and foundation issues are common). Always pull comps within a half-mile radius and within the last six months. If comps are sparse, expand your radius cautiously and adjust for differences in condition and square footage. Our guide on [How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) walks you through the full process step by step.
The best real estate deals aren't found in the hottest markets — they're found where other investors aren't looking. Bismarck is that market right now.
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Eyeing Bismarck
Investing remotely in a market you've never visited comes with real risks. Here's how to reduce them and position yourself to win deals in Bismarck without being on the ground full time.

items: Build a local team first: Find a property manager, a real estate attorney familiar with ND contracts, and a local contractor before you make your first offer. Bismarck is small enough that referrals from one professional often lead to others quickly.
Understand North Dakota's landlord-tenant laws: ND is generally considered a landlord-friendly state, with reasonable notice requirements and straightforward eviction processes.
Factor in winter maintenance costs: Budget $1,500 to $3,000 per year for snow removal, heating system maintenance, and winter-specific repairs. These costs catch out-of-state investors off guard.

Use data tools to find motivated sellers: AI-powered platforms like AIWholesail can help you identify distressed properties and off-market opportunities in Bismarck without needing to cold-call or drive for dollars.
Visit at least once before buying: A single trip to walk the neighborhoods and meet your local team will teach you more than any amount of remote research.
Start with a duplex or small multifamily: Bismarck has a decent supply of duplexes in the $250,000 to $350,000 range that offer natural vacancy hedging for remote owners.
Connect with the Bismarck-Mandan Board of Realtors and local REIA groups: There's a small but active investor community here, and local relationships surface deals faster than any marketing campaign.

Is Bismarck ND the Right Market for You?

Bismarck won't make you rich overnight. It's not a speculative boom market, and it's not trying to be. What it offers is stability, affordability, low investor competition, and a local economy built on foundations that don't disappear with the next economic cycle. For investors who are tired of overpaying in saturated markets and fighting 20 other buyers for every deal, Bismarck represents something genuinely valuable: a chance to buy right, operate efficiently, and build equity without the noise.
